newsitem.title: ITALY: SAI still in spotlight, Premafin higher.
newsitem.headline: SAI still in spotlight, Premafin higher.

text.p: Italy's largest motor insurance group Societa' Assicuratrice Industriale (SAI) remained in the spotlight on the Milan bourse on Monday with shares of its largest shareholder Premafin rising sharply.

Takeover speculation has surrounded SAI since its chairman and managing director both became involved in a bribes scandal, and renewed market talk has suggested that insurance giant Generali may strike.
On Friday, SAI confirmed that its chairman Salvatore Ligresti and managing director Fausto Rapisarda were resigning and added that it would announce their replacements within the next 10 days.

Ligesti's holding group Premafin holds 43.8 percent of SAI, while French state-controlled insurer GAN has around 10 percent. Late Friday, Premafin denied that there was any basis for speculation about a sale of SAI.
A Premafin official also called the idea of a sale of SAI "without any foundation", and added: "No negotiations have been started with anyone for the sale of the stake."

But speculation over the future of the Turin-based group has refused to die and SAI shares have ticked higher, while Premafin shares have risen strongly, especially since the Ligresti and Rapisarda sentences were confirmed by an appeals court in Rome earlier this month.

Italian insurance watchdog Isvap had demanded Ligresti and Rapisarda step down after they were found guilty of corruption charges relating to bribes paid by SAI to win an insurance contract from state energy group ENI.
By 1540 GMT, SAI shares had risen 0.9 percent to 13,960 lire while Premafin stock rose 9.8 percent to 646 lire in a generally lower Milan share market.

Analysts said SAI was a quality company with good management, and in its position as leader in Italy's motor insurance sector it would make a good fit with Generali, although they noted that Generali had made no official comment on the issue.
